interpretations: Per-patient ratio = average of HGB/HCT across that patient's lab rows (row-level ratios with NULLs ignored, then averaged per patient). The cross-patient average is the mean of these per-patient ratios, and the output is the mean of per-patient average PIC, the mean of ratios, and the mean excess for patients above that average
Per-patient ratio = AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT) over that patient's rows. The cross-patient average is the mean of these per-patient ratios
Per-patient ratio = SUM(HGB)/SUM(HCT) over that patient's rows. The cross-patient average is the mean of these per-patient ratios

Every lab row counts as a "patient record", so the cross-patient average is the mean of all row-level ratios (weighted by row count, not by patient). Patients are then selected by comparing their ratio to that average
Ignoring missing values means excluding rows where either HGB or HCT is NULL. PIC is averaged over the same filtered rows
Ignoring missing values means excluding rows where either HGB or HCT is NULL. PIC is averaged over all of the patient's rows, including those where HGB or HCT is NULL
Ignoring missing values means excluding rows where HGB, HCT, or PIC is NULL. All three measures use the same rows
HCT = 0 rows are excluded to avoid division by zero
Patients whose ratio is strictly above the cross-patient average are included. A patient equal to the average is excluded
Patients whose ratio is greater than or equal to the cross-patient average are included
The cross-patient average is computed over all patients with a valid ratio, including those with no PIC values
The cross-patient average is computed only over patients with both a valid ratio and a non-NULL PIC
Mean of average PIC = the average of each qualifying patient's own average PIC (a patient-level mean). The result is one row with three columns
Mean of average PIC = the average of PIC over all qualifying patients' lab rows pooled together (a row-level mean)
Mean of ratios = the average of the qualifying patients' ratios. Mean excess = that mean minus the cross-patient average. The two are equivalent in value but differ in how they are derived
Mean excess is computed as the average of (patient ratio − cross-patient average) over the qualifying patients, as a signed difference. It is always positive under the strict-greater reading
Only patients present in the Patient table are included, joining Laboratory to Patient. Laboratory rows with no matching Patient row are excluded
Only Laboratory rows are used, and patients are identified by Laboratory.ID. No join to Patient or Examination is made
The ratio is expressed as HGB divided by HCT. A reading that reverses it (HCT/HGB) is not intended
Patients with a NULL average PIC (all PIC values missing) among the qualifying group are ignored in the PIC mean, but still count in the ratio means
Patients with a NULL average PIC among the qualifying group are dropped from all three means
Missing interpretations:
Patients are grouped by Laboratory.ID, and the per-patient ratio is the median of that patient's row-level HGB/HCT ratios
The per-patient ratio uses only the patient's most recent lab row (latest Date)
The cross-patient average is the median of the per-patient ratios, not the mean

The cross-patient average is computed only over the patients who have non-NULL PIC and a valid ratio, and the qualifying set is then selected against this average (this differs from the existing PIC-based reading only if the qualifying set is not also restricted)
The mean excess is the average absolute difference (ratio − cross-patient average), expressed as a percentage of the cross-patient average
The output is the mean of PIC over qualifying rows, where PIC is taken from the same row-level ratios (not a per-patient average), with the ratio pooled at the row level
The ratio is computed with integer division (no decimal conversion), so the HGB/HCT values are truncated
HCT NULL or 0 is treated as missing, and HGB = 0 rows are excluded as invalid
queries:
WITH per_patient AS (
    SELECT ID,
           AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic,
           AVG(HGB * 1.0 / HCT) AS ratio
    FROM Laboratory
    WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0
    GROUP BY ID
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM per_patient
)
SELECT
    (SELECT AVG(avg_pic) FROM per_patient) AS mean_avg_pic,
    (SELECT avg_ratio FROM overall) AS mean_ratio,
    (SELECT AVG(p.ratio - o.avg_ratio)
     FROM per_patient p, overall o
     WHERE p.ratio > o.avg_ratio) AS mean_excess;
SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM (SELECT AVG(HGB) / AVG(HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID)
SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM (SELECT ID, SUM(HGB) * 1.0 / SUM(HCT) AS ratio FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID);
SELECT AVG(PIC) FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL
